title: Automation Templates Marketplace
description: Package Joe's automation consulting knowledge into reusable templates and workflows sold as digital products. Could include: LaunchAgent templates, cron job configurations, data transformation scripts, Slack bot setups, monitoring dashboards. Low effort per unit ($10-50 each), infinite scalability. Use Gumroad or Lemon Squeezy for distribution. Each consulting engagement could generate a template as a byproduct.

evaluation.notes: Strong passive income candidate with proven expertise edge. Can be byproduct of consulting engagements. Infinite scalability via digital distribution. Main challenge: differentiate via consulting experience + bundle/community angle.

title: Even Us Up: B2B Expense Splitting for Small Teams
description: Pivot Even Us Up from consumer expense sharing to also target small businesses — co-working spaces, consulting teams, shared offices, roommate houses with shared utilities. Premium features: receipt OCR scanning, tax categorization, QuickBooks/Wave integration, recurring splits, PDF export for accountants. B2B customers pay more and churn less than consumer users.
revenueModel: Freemium: free for personal, $4.99/mo per team for business features
rejectedReason: Limited differentiation vs Wave/QuickBooks; high support burden (multi-API integrations) reduces passive potential; unvalidated GTM path

researchEvidence.finding: Venn.ca and other fintech platforms actively promote Interac e-Transfer for business payments; market demand confirmed. However, Wave, QuickBooks dominate SMB expense management with established customer bases.

title: Personal AI OS Platform (Alfred-as-a-Service)
description: Joe is building a sophisticated personal AI operating system (OpenClaw + Command Center + cron + notifications + multi-channel). This stack could be productized for other solopreneurs, consultants, and small business owners who want their own 'Alfred'. Sell the pickaxes during the gold rush. Could start as a self-hosted open-source project with paid managed hosting, or a SaaS with customizable AI agent templates.
revenueModel: SaaS ($29-99/mo) or managed hosting ($49-199/mo per instance)

evaluation.notes: Joe has a genuine edge here — he built and runs this stack daily, and his consulting background mirrors the target market. Productizing is high effort, but SaaS/managed hosting offers strong passive revenue potential. Main risk is support overhead and onboarding complexity for non-technical users; a self-hosted open-source entry point would reduce friction and build community before monetizing.

title: Proactive Passive Income Opportunity Detector
description: AI agent that continuously scans market gaps, new platforms, trends in Joe's expertise areas (automation, trading, SaaS) and proactively suggests ideas with market size + effort estimates.

title: Client Automation Ideas Pipeline
description: Extract automation pain points from consulting engagements and turn them into product ideas or consulting upsells. Build a structured pipeline: observation → research → prototype → pitch.

evaluation.notes: Strong fit with Joe's consulting workflow and a clear unfair advantage because pain points come directly from real client work. The observation→research→prototype→pitch flow creates repeatable upsell and product discovery leverage with moderate build effort. Passive upside is moderate (not pure passive), but this can systematically feed higher-margin offers and future product bets.

title: Quiet-Hours Outbox + Morning Digest Dispatcher
description: Audit finding: quiet-hours policy blocks direct messaging but proactive jobs still generate results. Improvement: implement a durable outbox that captures overnight updates/questions and auto-delivers a structured morning digest at 09:00 AST. Include dedup, priority buckets (critical vs normal), and expiry rules for stale notices. Integrations: notification routing + Command Center feed + cron-event pipelines. Expected impact: fewer dropped updates, better signal quality, lower daytime interruption cost.

evaluation.notes: Real pattern with proven demand (Batch, SuprSend, NotificationAPI, Boomerang all implement quiet-hours + digest batching). Strong fit for Alfred's infrastructure and Joe's async-first workflow. Medium effort (2-3 weeks MVP: durable outbox table, dedup logic, morning cron sender, Command Center UI). Main constraint: this is internal optimization with zero passive revenue potential — not a business idea. Best implemented as an Alfred system improvement, not pursued as a product. Score: 6.8/10 (below 7-point promotion threshold).

researchEvidence.finding: Quiet-hours + digest batching is an industry-standard pattern. Evidence: Batch (batch.com) offers 'Quiet Hours for Email Trigger Automations'; SuprSend docs recommend batching + digest strategies; NotificationAPI supports digest delivery; Boomerang for Gmail popularized 'Inbox Pause' batched delivery. Demand is validated.
